elyse: Quick share of streaming vs non-streaming perf across GPUs/regions — ran an end-to-end harness yesterday, attaching quick numbers and a couple of charts. TL;DR: streaming gains latency for long-tail tokens but eats throughput at high concurrency on H100 when using flash kernels.

sam: Nice, can you paste the numbers?

elyse: Sure, here's the summary (all tests: gpt-small-ish model, 2k context, max_new_tokens=512, mixed-quant fp16->int8 experiment toggled). Batch sizing: non-stream = batch_size 8, streaming = concurrent_clients 64 with single-token flushing.

elyse: Region: us-west1, GPU: A100 80GB -> non-stream throughput 18.5k tokens/s, p95 latency 220ms; streaming throughput 15.2k tokens/s, p95 latency 160ms.

sam: So streaming improved p95 by ~60ms but throughput drops ~18%?

elyse: Exactly. For eu-west1 on H100: non-stream 24.8k tok/s, p95 190ms; streaming 19.4k tok/s, p95 125ms. H100 shows larger throughput hit with streaming when kernel=flash-attn.

matthew: Did you try cutlass kernels on H100?

elyse: Yes — cutlass + grouped gemm reduced streaming throughput drop: streaming 21.8k tok/s vs 24.8k non-stream (12% drop) and p95 135ms. So kernel choice matters.

zara: What about smaller GPUs (T4) and quantization?

elyse: T4 (europe) non-stream 6.3k tok/s p95 420ms; streaming 5.9k tok/s p95 380ms. int8 quant gave +30-35% throughput on T4 with small latency regression (~+10ms p95) for both modes.

sam: How about region variance? ap-southeast1 vs us-west1?

elyse: ap-southeast1 H100 had slightly worse p95 overall (network ~25ms extra), so end-to-end p95 for streaming bumped by that delta. Throughput numbers were within 5% of us-west when local infra identical.

matthew: Any charts / artifacts?

elyse: Uploaded two charts to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/1768123456/stream-vs-nonstream-rt.png and throughput_vs_concurrency.csv with raw samples. Also attached the harness command: ```python
# simplified harness snippet
run_bench(model='gpt-xx', gpu='h100', region='us-west1', mode='streaming', concurrency=64, kernels=['flash','cutlass'], quant='int8')
```

zara: Did you measure token-level tail (p99) or just p95?

elyse: p99 included — streaming p99 was still better in almost all H100/A100 runs (p99 drop ~120-200ms) until concurrency >128 where batching efficiency collapses. Non-stream sometimes has better amortized throughput at high concurrency because of larger micro-batches per request.

sam: Any guidance for capacity planning? say we need 100k tokens/s steady across us-west for a chat product with 90th pct latency <200ms

elyse: Quick back-of-envelope: pick H100 with cutlass kernels + int8: per-GPU sustained non-stream ~24k tok/s, streaming ~22k tok/s. So need ~5 GPUs (24k * 4 = 96k) non-stream, 5 GPUs streaming gives ~110k with lower p95. But account for headroom and failures -> recommend 6 reserved GPUs for Dedicated.

matthew: Any differences in socket protocols? SSE vs WebSocket for streaming endpoint?

elyse: Minor differences at infra layer. WebSocket had ~5-10ms better p95 in our tests due to fewer HTTP churns, but SSE simpler to scale with our load balancer. Implementation tradeoffs: WebSocket needs sticky routing for KV cache locality unless you propagate session state.

sam: Good point about KV locality. Did you test prefix cache hit rates across reconnects?

elyse: Yes — streaming reconnects without sticky session lose KV cache and p95 doubles for first request. With sticky session or shared cache layer, impact disappears. We noted this in the run notes.

zara: Any quality regressions when using int8?

elyse: Minor BLEU-style delta on eval set for some prompts (0.6-0.9% absolute) — we flagged a small set of prompts where sampling changed. Recommend running the prompt-level evals before rollout; Redwood Optimize has a quickship config to run those.

perf-bot: [auto-report] Full matrix results uploaded: /artifacts/1768123456/matrix.json, p95_table.csv, kernel_comparison.xlsx

sam: Awesome. Next steps: 1) add H100+cutlass as recommended profile in model-catalog for chat workloads, 2) add sticky-cookie option to streaming proxy, 3) run a dedicated int8 eval sweep on the regen prompts.

elyse: I'll open the PR for the model-catalog entry and a follow-up issue for proxy sticky-cookie. Thanks all :rocket:

matthew: Thanks — looks actionable.

zara: Thanks, really helpful.
